title: Conjecture 2
statement_text: For every hereditary class $C$ of structures, FO model checking is FPT on $C$ if and only if $C$ is monadically dependent.
context_text: This conjecture (cited as [28, Conjecture 8.2]) underpins the paper's notion of delineation: a class $C$ is delineated by twin-width if, for every hereditary closure $D$ of a subclass of $C$, $D$ has bounded twin-width if and only if $D$ is monadically dependent, which would confirm Conjecture 2 within $C$. The paper proves effective delineation for interval graphs and rooted directed path graphs, thereby settling Conjecture 2 for all hereditary subclasses of those classes.
paper_contribution: Proves Conjecture 2 for all hereditary subclasses of interval graphs and rooted directed path graphs by establishing that these classes are effectively delineated by twin-width; also shows Conjecture 2 cannot be settled this way for directed path graphs (multiple roots), axis-parallel two-lengthed segment graphs, and visibility graphs of simple polygons.
notes: Attributed to [28, Conjecture 8.2] in the paper; the exact authors of reference [28] cannot be determined from the provided text extract. The paper says 'see for instance', suggesting this is a known community conjecture with multiple attributions.

title: Open Question (unit segment graphs delineation)
statement_text: Are unit segment graphs delineated (by twin-width)?
context_text: Unit segment graphs are the intersection graphs of segments of length $1$ in the plane (any directions). Twin-width is a graph parameter defined via contraction sequences (iteratively merging two vertices, recording inconsistent adjacencies as red edges; twin-width at most $d$ means the graph can be reduced to one vertex keeping red degree at most $d$); classes of bounded twin-width are monadically dependent. A class is monadically dependent if it does not first-order transduce the class of all finite graphs (a transduction colours the vertices with a bounded number of unary predicates and defines a new graph by a first-order formula); it is conjectured that these are exactly the hereditary classes with fixed-parameter tractable first-order model checking, so that an effective form of delineation of $\mathcal{C}$ settles which hereditary subclasses of $\mathcal{C}$ have FPT model checking. A class $\mathcal{C}$ is delineated (by twin-width) if for every hereditary closure $\mathcal{D}$ of a subclass of $\mathcal{C}$, $\mathcal{D}$ has bounded twin-width if and only if $\mathcal{D}$ is monadically dependent. The authors prove that interval graphs and rooted directed path graphs are delineated, while segment graphs, directed path graphs, visibility graphs of simple polygons and even intersection graphs of axis-parallel segments with two distinct lengths are not. Towards the frontier, they show that $K_{t,t}$-free segment graphs and axis-parallel $H_t$-free unit segment graphs have bounded twin-width, where $H_t$ is the half-graph of height $t$ (vertices $a_1,\dots,a_t,b_1,\dots,b_t$ with $a_ib_j$ an edge iff $i\le j$, both sides independent) and freeness is with respect to semi-induced subgraphs (only edges between the two sides are prescribed); in contrast axis-parallel $H_4$-free two-lengthed segment graphs have unbounded twin-width, and (triangle-free) pure axis-parallel unit segment graphs were already known to have unbounded twin-width. The authors also ask the same question for visibility graphs of 1.5D terrains and for tournaments.
notes: Stated verbatim in the abstract: 'We leave as an open question whether unit segment graphs are delineated.'
